## Dataset: Öffentliche Beleuchtung der Stadt Zürich

Öffentliche Beleuchtungsstellen (Leuchten) der Stadt Zürich: Strassen- und Wegbeleuchtung, Beleuchtung für die Schifffahrt, Spezialbeleuchtung (Objekt-, Kunst- und Schmuckbeleuchtung).

Kontakt für Datenbezug: NetzKundenAnliegen@ewz.ch

**Zweck**: Dokumentation der Beleuchtungsstellen

**Genereller Hinweis zum Geodatensatz:**


Weitere Informationen zu diesem Datensatz finden sie unter [«**Öffentliche Beleuchtung der Stadt Zürich»** auf Geocat.ch](https://www.geocat.ch/geonetwork/srv/ger/catalog.search#/metadata/7125f956-6d11-4a69-946f-0f2480fc13e0).				
			   

**Datenerfassung:**

Die Standorte der Leuchtstellen in der Stadt Zürich werden im Feld mittels Tachymeter und GPS erfasst. Die Einmessungsdaten werden anschliessend in die Smallworld GIS Applikation Strom eingelesen und mit den Strom-Werkleitungsdaten verknüpft.

**Datengrundlage:**

Vermessungsbasis: Amtliche Vermessung der Stadt Zürich

# Load packages

```{r}
library(httr2)
library(sf)
library(skimr)
library(tidyverse)
library(xml2)
```

```{r}
# Identifies requests from this notebook in the OpenDataZurich access logs.
# Used explicitly by httr2 pipelines below; also picked up by sf::st_read via
# base R's HTTPUserAgent option.
USER_AGENT <- "OpenDataZurich-StarterCode-Notebook/1.0 (lang=r; +https://github.com/opendatazurich/starter-code)"
options(HTTPUserAgent = USER_AGENT)
# sf::st_read fetches via GDAL/curl, which uses this env var.
Sys.setenv(GDAL_HTTP_USERAGENT = USER_AGENT)
```

# Load the data

data link
```{r}
url <- "https://www.stadt-zuerich.ch/geodaten/download/Oeffentliche_Beleuchtung_der_Stadt_Zuerich?format=geojson_link"
```


Helper function to create the url based on the geoportal, as the files are not directly available via a fixed link like csvs.
```{r}
get_geoportal_url <- function(url) {
  dataset_identifier <- sub(".*/(.*)\\?.*", "\\1", url)
  paste0("https://www.ogd.stadt-zuerich.ch/wfs/geoportal/", dataset_identifier)
}
```

```{r}
# Helper function to get available layers from WFS
get_wfs_layers <- function(url) {
  
  url_geoportal <- get_geoportal_url(url)
  
  cat("Getting available layers from:", url_geoportal, "\n")
  
  # read xml from geoportal
  resp <- request(url_geoportal) |>
    req_user_agent(USER_AGENT) |>
    req_headers(service = "WFS", version = "1.1.0", request = "GetCapabilities") |>
    req_perform()
  
  content_as_xml <- resp_body_xml(resp)
  
  # find available layers: find "Name" nodes with parent "Layer"
  name_nodes <- content_as_xml |> xml_ns_strip() |> xml_find_all("//Name")
  
  # keep all nodes that have Name and whose parent's name is "Layer"
  # and directly extract the name to get a list of typenames
  typename_nodes <- purrr::keep(name_nodes,
                                \(x) xml_name(xml_parent(x)) == "Layer")
  
  return(typename_nodes)
}

# Fetch available layers
layers <- get_wfs_layers(url)

# Set first layer as default
typename <- xml_text(layers[[1]])
cat("Chosen typename:", typename, "\n")
```

read the data
```{r}
read_geodata <- function(url, typename) {
  url_geoportal <- get_geoportal_url(url)
  
  request <- request(url_geoportal) |>
    req_url_query(
      service = "WFS",
      version = "1.1.0",
      outputFormat = "GeoJSON",
      request = "GetFeature",
      typename = typename
    )
  
  st_read(request$url)
}

df <- read_geodata(url, typename)
```

```{r overview}
tibble(
  rows = nrow(df),
  columns = ncol(df),
  duplicate_rows_after_first = sum(duplicated(df))
)
glimpse(df)
head(df)
```

## plotting maps

base R plot

```{r}
plot(df$geometry)
```

ggplot2 plot
```{r}
df |>
  ggplot() +

```

## Missing values

```{r missing-values}
missing <- tibble(
  column = names(df),
  missing = map_int(df, ~ sum(is.na(.x))),
  missing_pct = map_dbl(df, ~ mean(is.na(.x)) * 100)
) |>
  arrange(desc(missing_pct))
missing

# Show up to 20 columns with missing values; percentages use all rows.
missing_plot <- missing |> filter(missing > 0) |> slice_head(n = 20)
if (nrow(missing_plot) > 0) {
  ggplot(missing_plot, aes(x = missing_pct, y = reorder(column, missing_pct))) +
    geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
    scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 100)) +
    labs(x = "Missing values (%)", y = NULL, title = "Missingness by column")
} else {
  message("No missing values to plot (or the dataset has no rows).")
}
```

## Summary and distributions

`skim()` reports completeness and type-specific summaries. Inspect units before interpreting numeric codes as measurements.

```{r summary}
if (nrow(df) > 0 && ncol(df) > 0) {
  skim(st_drop_geometry(df))
} else {
  message("No data to summarize.")
}
```

```{r histograms}
# Plot up to four numeric columns, excluding non-finite values only from plots.
numeric_names <- names(select(df, where(is.numeric))) |> head(4)
for (column in numeric_names) {
  values <- df[[column]]
  values <- values[is.finite(values)]
  if (length(values) > 0) {
    plot <- ggplot(tibble(value = values), aes(x = value)) +
      geom_histogram(bins = 30, fill = "steelblue", colour = "white") +
      labs(title = column, x = column, y = "Count")
    print(plot)
  }
}
```

```{r category-counts}
# Top 10 values for up to three categorical columns, including missing values.
categorical_names <- df |>
  select(where(~ is.character(.x) || is.factor(.x) || is.logical(.x))) |>
  names() |>
  head(3)
for (column in categorical_names) {
  cat(column, "\n")
  df |> count(.data[[column]], sort = TRUE) |> head(10) |> print()
}
```
